D19·ya9x — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.2 lane pool: lanes are linked worktrees at `<state base>/<clone key>/lanes/lane-<k>`, created on first use, kept across runs and initiatives, each marked to serve the checkout's record (D18). A driver holds a flock per lane (`lane-<k>.lock`, the run lock's primitive) and skips lanes another driver holds. Deps: a setup command (`--lane-setup`, else npm ci / pnpm / yarn / bun from the checkout's lockfile) runs in a lane only when its stamp in the lane's gitdir (command + lockfile sha256) differs. `run_started.lanes` (integer ≥2) is recorded; a resume keeps the recorded count; `--lanes 1` takes today's code path with nothing recorded.
over: A sibling `<repo>.lanes/` dir; lanes inside the checkout; one pool per initiative; recording lane paths on run_started; reinstalling deps every run.
because: The state dir is the repo's per-clone home outside the tree (state-dir.ts), so vitest, tsc and rg never see N copies and the operator's parent dir stays clean. Per-lane locks let runs of different initiatives share one warm pool without colliding. A path is machine-local and the record is shared, so only the count is recorded. The lockfile stamp is what makes the install happen once.
